name: How do you eliminate pet and moisture odors trapped in a foreclosed home's floor?

mainEntity.name: How do you eliminate pet and moisture odors trapped in a foreclosed home's floor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Severe pet urine and standing moisture odors must be addressed directly at the subfloor level before any new flooring is laid. Tearing out contaminated carpet and pad is just the first step; animal urine frequently soaks into plywood or concrete foundations. In our rehab work across the Denver area, we treat exposed subflooring with heavy-duty enzymatic cleaners and apply specialized oil-based or shellac primers to seal in odors permanently. If the subfloor has rotted from long-term dampness, we cut away the affected boards and frame in new structural backing before flooring goes down.
acceptedAnswer.description: Remove old materials, treat the exposed subfloor with enzyme cleaners, seal the surface with specialized primers, or replace rotted wood before installing new flooring.
